answers.q1: Ruby with Bundler (Rake for tasks). From the repo root, run `bundle install`. sinatra-contrib and rack-protection have their own Gemfiles, so CI also runs `bundle install` inside each of them: `(cd sinatra-contrib && bundle install)` and `(cd rack-protection && bundle install)`.
answers.q2: CI runs three separate suites, so there is no single command for everything. Core Sinatra (minitest): `bundle exec rake`. sinatra-contrib (rspec): `(cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rake)`. rack-protection: `(cd rack-protection && bundle exec rake)`. To run all three in one line: `bundle exec rake && (cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rake) && (cd rack-protection && bundle exec rake)`.
answers.q3: `(cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rspec spec/capture_spec.rb)`. sinatra-contrib uses RSpec, and its Gemfile and .rspec are in that directory, so the command has to run from there.
answers.q4: CI (.github/workflows/test.yml) has no lint or formatting step, so there is no CI command for this. The repo does have RuboCop set up: the root Gemfile pins rubocop ~> 1.32.0 and there is a .rubocop.yml. The command to run it is `bundle exec rubocop`. The config excludes test/**, rack-protection/** and sinatra-contrib/**, so it only checks the root lib/ and Rakefile code.
answers.q5: I found no committed generated or vendored code. Things you shouldn't edit by hand: `coverage/`, `doc/` (including `doc/api`, generated by yardoc), `.yardoc`, `pkg/` and `*.gem` build output, `*.lock` files such as Gemfile.lock, and `vendor/` (including `vendor/bundle`). All of these are in .gitignore. The `VERSION` file is also normally changed only through the release process (see RELEASING.md).

q1.reason: Gives `bundle install` with Bundler and correctly notes the sub-project Gemfiles.

q2.reason: Gives `bundle exec rake` for core and also correctly covers the sinatra-contrib and rack-protection suites.

q3.reason: `(cd sinatra-contrib && bundle exec rspec spec/capture_spec.rb)` matches the accepted command.

q4.reason: States CI has no lint step and gives `bundle exec rubocop` as the local command.
